newsitem.title: USA: Dole camp hits back at 'Trainspotting' ad.
newsitem.headline: Dole camp hits back at 'Trainspotting' ad.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole struck back on Saturday at an advertisement mocking him for his criticism of the movie "Trainspotting", which he had said promoted heroin.
In the ad, a smiling Dole appears in a mock campaign poster placed in a Los Angeles newspaper by Capitol Records, which is releasing the soundtrack album for the controversial British movie.
Dole made headlines earlier this month when he accused "Trainspotting" and "Pulp Fiction" -- two movies he admitted not seeing -- of glorifying drug abuse.
The ad depicts Dole with a large lapel badge reading "Iggy Pop For President." The punk veteran's song "Lust For Life" is on the soundtrack and is featured prominently in the movie.

Dole's press secretary, Nelson Warfield, said "nothing better illustrates the need for corporate responsibility in the entertainment industry than this glib and whimsical ad for the soundtrack from a movie that glamorizes heroin use."
He added in a statement, "Like Bill Clinton himself, too many entertainment industry executives seem to think that drug abuse is something to laugh about."
The advertisement ran just once in the LA Weekly, a Los Angeles publication that comes out on Thursdays, a record label spokeswoman said.
"I would say it's a tribute (to Dole)," said Faith Henschel, Capitol's vice-president of marketing who designed the ad, in an interview. "It's not meant to be mean-spirited."
